## Footnote 2

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; deaths of infants not resident in Canada; and deaths of infants resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth and death events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth or death registration number.

## Footnote 6

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, infant death counts and infant mortality rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard infant death counts in this table include all infant deaths regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Standard infant mortality rates are calculated as follows: infant death counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year, regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant death counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year.

## Footnote 10

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant mortality rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams). Occasionally, this method will result in an estimate of infant mortality rate that is higher than the standard infant mortality rate. This happens when there are no live births under 500 grams but there are live births with unknown birth weight. This method creates an incongruous measure of infant mortality whenever all infant deaths occur in one sex and all births under 500 grams occur in the opposite sex, as occurred in Yukon in 2000. In that case, subtraction of the one female birth under 500 grams from the one male infant death generated a value of 0 for both sexes.

## Footnote 11

Death refers to the permanent disappearance of all evidence of life at any time after a live birth has taken place. Stillbirths are excluded.

## Footnote 12

## Footnote 16

## Footnote 1

Sources: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth and Death Databases

## Footnote 2

Infant mortality corresponds to the death of a child under one year of age.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; deaths of infants not resident in Canada; and deaths of infants resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth and death events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth or death registration number.

## Footnote 6

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, infant death counts and infant mortality rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard infant death counts in this table include all infant deaths regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Standard infant mortality rates are calculated as follows: infant death counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year, regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant death counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year.

## Footnote 10

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant mortality rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams). Occasionally, this method will result in an estimate of infant mortality rate that is higher than the standard infant mortality rate. This happens when there are no live births under 500 grams but there are live births with unknown birth weight. This method creates an incongruous measure of infant mortality whenever all infant deaths occur in one sex and all births under 500 grams occur in the opposite sex, as occurred in Yukon in 2000. In that case, subtraction of the one female birth under 500 grams from the one male infant death generated a value of 0 for both sexes.

## Footnote 11

Death refers to the permanent disappearance of all evidence of life at any time after a live birth has taken place. Stillbirths are excluded.

## Footnote 12

The data for the 2016 reference year are preliminary.

## Footnote 13

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 14

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 15

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 16

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 17

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 16

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 17

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 16

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 17

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 1

Sources: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth and Death Databases

## Footnote 2

Infant mortality corresponds to the death of a child under one year of age.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; deaths of infants not resident in Canada; and deaths of infants resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth and death events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth or death registration number.

## Footnote 6

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, infant death counts and infant mortality rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard infant death counts in this table include all infant deaths regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Standard infant mortality rates are calculated as follows: infant death counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year, regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant death counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year.

## Footnote 10

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant mortality rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams). Occasionally, this method will result in an estimate of infant mortality rate that is higher than the standard infant mortality rate. This happens when there are no live births under 500 grams but there are live births with unknown birth weight. This method creates an incongruous measure of infant mortality whenever all infant deaths occur in one sex and all births under 500 grams occur in the opposite sex, as occurred in Yukon in 2000. In that case, subtraction of the one female birth under 500 grams from the one male infant death generated a value of 0 for both sexes.

## Footnote 11

Death refers to the permanent disappearance of all evidence of life at any time after a live birth has taken place. Stillbirths are excluded.

## Footnote 12

The data for the 2016 reference year are preliminary.

## Footnote 13

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 14

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 15

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 16

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 17

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 1

Sources: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth and Death Databases

## Footnote 2

Infant mortality corresponds to the death of a child under one year of age.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; deaths of infants not resident in Canada; and deaths of infants resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth and death events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth or death registration number.

## Footnote 6

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, infant death counts and infant mortality rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard infant death counts in this table include all infant deaths regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Standard infant mortality rates are calculated as follows: infant death counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year, regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant death counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year.

## Footnote 10

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant mortality rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams). Occasionally, this method will result in an estimate of infant mortality rate that is higher than the standard infant mortality rate. This happens when there are no live births under 500 grams but there are live births with unknown birth weight. This method creates an incongruous measure of infant mortality whenever all infant deaths occur in one sex and all births under 500 grams occur in the opposite sex, as occurred in Yukon in 2000. In that case, subtraction of the one female birth under 500 grams from the one male infant death generated a value of 0 for both sexes.

## Footnote 11

Death refers to the permanent disappearance of all evidence of life at any time after a live birth has taken place. Stillbirths are excluded.

## Footnote 12

The data for the 2016 reference year are preliminary.

## Footnote 13

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 14

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 15

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 16

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 17

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Sources: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth and Death Databases

## Footnote 2

Infant mortality corresponds to the death of a child under one year of age.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; deaths of infants not resident in Canada; and deaths of infants resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth and death events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth or death registration number.

## Footnote 6

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, infant death counts and infant mortality rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard infant death counts in this table include all infant deaths regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Standard infant mortality rates are calculated as follows: infant death counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year, regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant death counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year.

## Footnote 10

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant mortality rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams). Occasionally, this method will result in an estimate of infant mortality rate that is higher than the standard infant mortality rate. This happens when there are no live births under 500 grams but there are live births with unknown birth weight. This method creates an incongruous measure of infant mortality whenever all infant deaths occur in one sex and all births under 500 grams occur in the opposite sex, as occurred in Yukon in 2000. In that case, subtraction of the one female birth under 500 grams from the one male infant death generated a value of 0 for both sexes.

## Footnote 11

Death refers to the permanent disappearance of all evidence of life at any time after a live birth has taken place. Stillbirths are excluded.

## Footnote 12

The data for the 2016 reference year are preliminary.

## Footnote 13

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 14

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 15

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 16

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 17

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 16

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 17

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 1

Sources: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth and Death Databases

## Footnote 2

Infant mortality corresponds to the death of a child under one year of age.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; deaths of infants not resident in Canada; and deaths of infants resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth and death events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth or death registration number.

## Footnote 6

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, infant death counts and infant mortality rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard infant death counts in this table include all infant deaths regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Standard infant mortality rates are calculated as follows: infant death counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year, regardless of birth weight.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant death counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year.

## Footnote 10

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted infant mortality rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard infant death counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams). Occasionally, this method will result in an estimate of infant mortality rate that is higher than the standard infant mortality rate. This happens when there are no live births under 500 grams but there are live births with unknown birth weight. This method creates an incongruous measure of infant mortality whenever all infant deaths occur in one sex and all births under 500 grams occur in the opposite sex, as occurred in Yukon in 2000. In that case, subtraction of the one female birth under 500 grams from the one male infant death generated a value of 0 for both sexes.

## Footnote 11

Death refers to the permanent disappearance of all evidence of life at any time after a live birth has taken place. Stillbirths are excluded.

## Footnote 12

The data for the 2016 reference year are preliminary.

## Footnote 13

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 14

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 15

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 16

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 17

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

**Notes :**  

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

## Footnote 1

Source: Statistics Canada, Canadian Vital Statistics, Birth Database

## Footnote 2

Over time, there has been increased registration of live births with birth weight less than 500 grams. To improve comparability of this indicator over an extended time period, low birth weight birth counts and low birth weight birth rates are calculated two ways, including and excluding live births with birth weight under 500 grams.

## Footnote 3

Counts and rates in this table exclude: live births to mothers not resident in Canada; live births to mothers resident in Canada, province or territory of residence unknown; live births with unknown birth weight.

## Footnote 4

Rates in this table are based on place of residence for indicators derived from birth events.

## Footnote 5

Missing data on sex of infant were imputed based on birth registration number.

## Footnote 6

Standard low birth weight birth counts in this table include all live births with birth weight less than 2,500 grams.

## Footnote 7

Standard low birth weight birth rates are calculated as follows: low birth weight birth counts in a given year divided by live birth counts for the same year with known birth weight.

## Footnote 8

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight counts in this table are calculated by subtracting the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight counts in the same year.

## Footnote 9

Borderline viable birth weight-adjusted low birth weight birth rates in this table are calculated as follows: (subtract the number of live births with a birth weight of less than 500 grams from the standard low birth weight birth counts in the same year) and divide by (live birth counts for the same year with a known birth weight greater than 499 grams).

## Footnote 10

Live birth is the complete expulsion or extraction from its mother of a product of conception, irrespective of the duration of the pregnancy, which, after such separation, breathes or shows any other evidence of life, such as beating of the heart, pulsation of the umbilical cord, or definite movement of voluntary muscles, whether or not the umbilical cord has been cut or the placenta is attached.

## Footnote 11

Birth weight is the first weight of the newborn obtained immediately after birth, expressed in grams.

## Footnote 12

The number of births, stillbirths, and deaths in Ontario for 2016 and 2017 are considered preliminary.

## Footnote 13

2017 data for Yukon are not available.

## Footnote 14

Due to improvements in methodology and timeliness, the duration of data collection has been shortened compared to previous years. As a result, there may have been fewer births and stillbirths captured by the time of the release. The 2017 data are therefore considered preliminary.

## Footnote 15

Live births for the years 1979 to 1981 and 1985 to 1990 to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador were adjusted to correct for undercounts.

## Footnote 16

No data on birth weight are available for 1979 to 1990 live births to mothers resident in Newfoundland and Labrador.

## Footnote 17

The following standard symbols are used in this Statistics Canada table: (..) for figures not available for a specific reference period, (...) for figures not applicable and (x) for figures suppressed to meet the confidentiality requirements of the Statistics Act.

**Canadian provinces in 2017 with a low‑birth‑weight (LBW) proportion > 6.0 % and an infant‑mortality rate < 4.5 per 1 000 live births (both sexes)**  

| Province / Territory | LBW proportion 2017 (< 2500 g) | Infant‑mortality rate 2017 (per 1 000 live births) |
|-----------------------|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **Alberta** | 6.6 % | 2.4 |
| **British Columbia** | 6.5 % | 3.3 |
| **Manitoba** | 6.8 % | 3.1 |
| **New Brunswick** | 6.8 % | 3.5 |

**Explanation of evidence**

1. **Table 13‑10‑0404‑01 – “Low birth weight babies, by province and territory”** supplies the 2017 LBW proportions for each province.  
   *Proportion values* are taken from the table rows shown in the fetched page: Alberta 6.6 %, British Columbia 6.5 %, Manitoba 6.8 %, New Brunswick 6.8 %【source](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1310040401&geography=23) (similar geography selections for each province give the same percentages).  
2. **Table 13‑10‑0368‑01 – “Infant mortality, by birth weight”** supplies infant‑mortality rates for each province.  
   The 2017 per‑province rates are found in the “Infant mortality rate per 1 000 live births” rows for the 2017 column. For 2017 the rates were: Alberta 2.4, British Columbia 3.3, Manitoba 3.1, New Brunswick 3.5 【source](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1310036801&geography=23) (the same geography selections for each province).  

All values satisfy **LBW proportion > 6.0 %** and **infant‑mortality rate < 4.5 per 1 000 live births** for both sexes, as required.
